data.title: Anthropic shares jump 17% on debut; Democrats call it 'Trojan Horse'
data.description:
Shares of Anthropic surged on their stock market debut on Thursday, ending the session nearly 17% above the IPO price as investors showed strong appetite for the artificial intelligence company despite concerns over the technology sector and reports surrounding Nvidia.

The stock settled at $97.17, compared with its IPO price of $83. It opened at $111.50 and climbed to an intraday high of $111.53, briefly pushing the company's market capitalisation close to $2 trillion. The valuation stood at approximately $1.76 trillion at the close.

The strong debut signals continued investor interest in the AI sector, even as questions persist over the sustainability of the industry's rapid expansion and the companies likely to emerge as long-term winners.

Michael Rosen, chief investment officer at Angeles Investments, said the IPO had generated strong demand and provided a near-term lift to sentiment across the AI ecosystem. He noted that demand for computing capacity remained robust, but said investors were increasingly distinguishing between companies with access to existing computing infrastructure and those dependent on further data centre expansion.

According to Rosen, hyperscalers with strong balance sheets and cash flows could be better placed to navigate this shift.

More than 20 banks participated in the IPO syndicate, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serving as lead underwriters. Brokerages have projected that the company's revenue could reach around $400 million by 2029.

The listing has also significantly increased the paper wealth of Anthropic's seven co-founders. According to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission dated November 10, Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish and Chris Olah each hold approximately 240 million to 244 million shares.

At the closing price of $97.17, the value of each founder's holding works out to roughly $23.3 billion to $23.7 billion.

Anthropic's strong debut came against a weaker backdrop for technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite fell nearly 2.3% during the session, with major technology companies also facing selling pressure. Alphabet declined 2.9%, while Amazon dropped close to 3.9%.

Founded in 2021 by Dario Amodei and a group of former OpenAI researchers, Anthropic has emerged as a major rival to its former parent company's AI business. The company develops the Claude family of AI models and has attracted scrutiny over its approach to AI safety, regulation and national security.

The blockbuster listing has also renewed calls among some US lawmakers for tighter oversight of the artificial intelligence industry.

US Representative Pramila Jayapal criticised the timing of the IPO, citing recent disruptions to critical systems. In a post on X, she questioned whether investors should be rewarding a company whose technology could pose risks involving cybersecurity and foreign adversaries.

Senator Chris Van Hollen also called for urgent action to address the potential risks associated with artificial intelligence. In a social media video, he said the IPO could benefit wealthy investors while leaving broader concerns about the technology unresolved.

data.title: Asian shares head for worst week since 2020 as AI trade gloom fails to abate
data.description:
Key points:
  • Asia stocks on track for worst week since March 2020
  • Anthropic's historic debut fails to revive faith in AI trade
  • Dollar holds near 19-month peak on haven flow

By Jiaxing Li

Asian shares slid on Friday to be on track for their worst week since 2020, as Anthropic's debut failed to restore investor faith in AI trades, while the dollar extended a rally on safe-haven flows.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares (.MIAP0000PUS) lost 2.5%, poised for a six-day losing streak. The gauge has now declined 7% this week, its worst performance since March 2020.

Japan's Nikkei tumbled 4.1% and was headed for a 6.8% weekly drop, while South Korea's KOSPI fell 4.7% and was set to end the week 7.5% lower.

The moves in Asia followed losses of more than 2% for the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX and the Nasdaq Composite .

Anthropic, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company, saw its shares surge more than 30% in a historic debut but the euphoria failed to lift other boats.

"Anthropic's blockbuster IPO proved not enough to assuage the overall concern about the outlook for the AI trade and equities more broadly," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

The wider AI sector has been bruised by the exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia as well as additional momentum for the anti-data-center movement in the wake of the Democrats' sweep of the US midterm elections.

Unease about mounting debt loads in the sector and warnings that AI threatens human extinction have also hit sentiment.

Rodda said that with the AI trade fading and Fed rate hikes seen likely, general market sentiment is shaky and the risk is that this bearishness begins to drag stocks even lower.

US stock futures also point to further losses, with the S&P 500 futures down 0.4% and Nasdaq futures down 0.7% in Asia on Friday.

DOLLAR EXTENDS RALLY, TREASURY YIELDS DIP ON RISK AVERSION

As risk sentiment took a beating, the US dollar extended its rally, also supported by growing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve.

The dollar index last traded steady at 103.86, after hitting its strongest level since April 2025 this week.

Fed funds futures imply that a quarter-point rate hike next month is essentially locked in, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.

In government debt, US Treasury yields eased as the sharp equity selloff pushed investors toward safe-haven bonds. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes held steady at 5.026%, near a one-week low. The two-year yield (US2YT=RR) touched 4.749%, compared with a US close of 4.779%.

Oil prices were mostly steady after an earlier spike, as reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz offset pressure from rising US crude inventories and forecasts for a global oil surplus. (O/R)

Brent crude futures settled flat at $91.98 a barrel, on track for a third straight week of decline.

Non-interest-bearing gold dipped 0.6% to $3,601.40 an ounce and was headed for a 7.3% weekly loss.

data.title: BOJ December Rate Hike Looks Likely After CPI Results — Market Talk
data.description: With Japan's consumer inflation picking up in October, a Bank of Japan rate hike at its next policy meeting in December looks highly likely, says Takeshi Minami, an economist at Norinchukin Research Institute. "The central bank will likely discuss an additional increase in March 2027, when inflation is expected to have accelerated into the 3% range," he adds. Minami expects energy costs, reflecting the effects of government policy changes, to drive inflation sharply higher in early 2027. Consumer prices excluding fresh food climbed 2.2% in October from a year earlier, following September's 2.1% gain, government data showed Friday. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)

data.title: Dollar near 19-month peak as AI jitters sap risk appetite
data.description:
By Li Gu and Rae Wee

The dollar held near a 19-month high on Friday, having risen over the past eight sessions as jitters over the AI trade sent investors fleeing to safe-haven assets, while the yen steadied after Japanese inflation data.

The dollar index was perched near the 103.9 level, its strongest since early April 2025, and was on track for a fourth straight week of gains. The rally accelerated on November 10, when hotter-than-expected US inflation data reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve would tighten policy. Markets are now pricing in a 25-basis-point hike in December and a small chance of a larger move.

The AI trade continued to set the mood, with Anthropic's historic market debut doing little to revive sentiment as US equities fell sharply overnight.

Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, edging past SpaceX's June listing and capping a volatile stretch for the AI sector that tested Wall Street's appetite for the technology.

"Risk aversion intensified, supporting the safe-haven dollar and driving demand for US Treasuries," OCBC analysts said in a note. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks."

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell to a one-week low of 5.016% in early Asia trade and is down 10 basis points on the week.

Adding to the dollar's strength were hawkish signals from the Fed. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that the evidence did not suggest inflation was heading back to 2% on its own, and that the booming rollout of AI technology could further boost inflation the Fed would have to counteract.

The yen edged up 0.1% against the dollar to 159.50. Data showed Japan's annual core inflation accelerated to 2.2% in October, staying above the central bank's 2% target for a second straight month and pointing to broadening price pressures that cement the case for a near-term rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

Sterling languished near a one-year low against the dollar at $1.3094, and the euro struggled near its lowest level since April 2025 and last bought $1.0972. The Aussie hovered close to a one-year low of $0.66476.

China's offshore yuan slipped 0.4% overnight, breaking from its recent pattern of calm moves, with no obvious catalyst. China left key benchmark lending rates unchanged in November for an 18th consecutive month.

data.title: Boston Scientific announces pricing of $3.0 billion and €4.25 billion offerings of senior notes
data.description:
MARLBOROUGH, Mass., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Boston Scientific Corporation (the "Company") () announced today that it has priced a public offering of $3,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of U.S. dollar-denominated notes (the "USD Offering"), consisting of $1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.375% Senior Notes due 2029, $750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.500% Senior Notes due 2031, $750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.750% Senior Notes due 2033 and $500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2036 (collectively, the "USD Notes").

In addition, the Company announced today that American Medical Systems Europe B.V., its indirect wholly owned finance subsidiary, has priced a public offering of €4,250,000,000 aggregate principal amount of euro-denominated notes (the "Euro Offering" and, together with the USD Offering, the "Offerings"), consisting of €500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Floating Rate Notes due 2028 (the "Floating Rate Notes"), €500,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 3.875% Senior Notes due 2028, €750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 4.125% Senior Notes due 2030, €750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 4.500% Senior Notes due 2034, €1,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 4.750% Senior Notes due 2038 and €750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.125% Senior Notes due 2046 (collectively with the Floating Rate Notes, the "Euro Notes"). The Euro Notes will be fully and unconditionally guaranteed by the Company.

The Offerings are being made pursuant to a registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The Offerings are expected to close on December 1, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Neither Offering is conditioned upon the completion of the other Offering. The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the Offerings, together with short-term borrowings and/or borrowings under its credit agreement(s) and cash on hand, to finance the cash consideration payable in connection with the acquisition of Penumbra, Inc. (the "Penumbra Acquisition") and to pay related fees and expenses and, to the extent that the net proceeds from the Offerings are not used for such purposes, for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, short term investments, reduction of short term debt, funding of working capital and potential future acquisitions.

The Offerings are not conditioned upon the completion of the Penumbra Acquisition. However, if the Penumbra Acquisition is not completed on or before the applicable special mandatory redemption end date, or if the applicable issuer notifies the trustee that the Company will not pursue completion of the Penumbra Acquisition, each series of the USD Notes and the Euro Notes, except for the Floating Rate Notes, will be subject to a special mandatory redemption at a redemption price equal to 101% of the aggregate principal amount of such series, plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, to, but excluding, the special mandatory redemption date.

Nothing herein shall constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy the securities, nor shall there be any sale of the securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to qualification under the securities laws of any such state or jurisdiction. data.title: CATL Opens Türkiye's First NING SERVICE Experience Center in Istanbul
data.description:
ISTANBUL, Türkiye, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CATL today announced the official launch of its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in Türkiye. The facility serves as the country's first dedicated battery depot repair center and integrated sales-and-service hub, marking a further step in expanding its localized new energy aftermarket service network and supporting the country's shift towards cleaner energy systems.

Türkiye sits at the crossroads of Europe, Asia and the Middle East — a regional economic hub with a fast-growing EV market and a rapidly expanding energy storage sector, where the shift toward clean energy is driving demand for specialized battery support. Its National Energy 2040 plan targets 20 million electric vehicles and 140 GWh of storage requirement by 2040. Against that backdrop, NING SERVICE is delivering full-lifecycle battery services on both the road and the grid, reinforcing the infrastructure that transition depends on.

Located in Istanbul, the NING SERVICE Experience Center represents an important milestone in the collaboration between CATL and Ascendum Türkiye, part of Ascendum Group, offering comprehensive full-lifecycle after-sales support, cultivating local technical talent and accelerating the deployment of advanced electrification and energy storage solutions.

Covering more than 1,200 square meters, the Istanbul center brings together service zones for battery testing, diagnosis, repair, maintenance and refurbishment, exhibition and retail space, training rooms and a customer lounge. The exhibition and retail area presents CATL's system-level capabilities across electric mobility and energy storage, including bedrock chassis, portable power stations, battery protection plates and integrated charging-and-storage units. The center serves as a localized service hub for the region and as a platform connecting partners across the ecosystem.

Providing a comprehensive new energy aftermarket service system

As CATL's independent aftermarket service brand, NING SERVICE delivers a one-stop, full-lifecycle battery service system that encompass battery diagnostics, repair, maintenance, refurbishment, training, recycling, aftermarket logistics and warehousing. Backed by CATL's deep R&D and extreme manufacturing capabilities, its services product categories from passenger and commercial vehicles to energy storage systems, setting a new benchmark for new energy service delivery in the region.

That capability is delivered through one of the industry's largest after-sales networks:

  • 1,429 professional service locations across more than 80 countries and regions, with the aim of reaching 100 countries and regions by 2027 and 10,000 service locations by 2030;
  • More than 9,900 service engineers and over 10,000 technicians certified for new energy after-sales service, with a 24-hour response mechanism in overseas markets;
  • Its deep-repair capability, delivered through a network of 95 centers, covers 76.8% of EV models and 90% of repair jobs;
  • The Intelligent Eagle Eye System, in use at more than 150 repair facilities, providing full traceability and quality control;
  • The Intelligent Battery Check System, supporting precise battery health diagnostics, slows battery aging by up to 9.5%;
  • More than 70 industry standards participated in or revised, and over 200 authorized patents worldwide

Strengthening local partnerships and service capabilities

CATL is extending its local footprint by strengthening infrastructure and building partnerships in the market. By combining CATL's technological expertise with Ascendum Group's 67 years of industrial heritage and robust local network, the Istanbul center enables CATL to serve clients throughout Türkiye, putting its know-how and rapid-response capability close to where batteries are actually in use.

The center anchors a network to all Türkiye and a team of CATL-certified engineers. It also serves as the network's training base, where technicians are trained and certified to CATL's standards before they work on customer batteries, building a local pool of battery service skills that the market will keep drawing on.

"The opening of Türkiye's first NING SERVICE Experience Center marks an important milestone in our strategic partnership with CATL and represents the first business initiative launched under Ascendum Green.Shift," said Tolga Polat, CEO of Ascendum Türkiye. "By combining CATL's advanced battery technologies with Ascendum's long-standing technical service expertise and customer-focused approach, we aim to provide reliable, high-quality aftermarket solutions across Türkiye. We are investing in local technical capabilities, developing specialized teams and strengthening our service infrastructure to meet the evolving needs of the energy and mobility sectors. Looking ahead, our goal is to gradually expand our service network nationwide and build a sustainable ecosystem that creates long-term value for our customers and supports Türkiye's energy transition."

"Türkiye has moved into the fast lane on electrification, and demand for aftermarket service will grow with it," said Bruce Li, Co-president of Sales & Marketing and President of Commercial Applications & Aftermarket Business of CATL. "As our first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country, it brings CATL's technology, our training standards and Ascendum's local reach together, so that customers on the road and on the grid are served by people and parts that are already here. From here, we will keep extending our service network across Türkiye, work in step with the country's National Energy 2040 goals, and give the energy transition the service backbone it needs to hold up over time."

Looking ahead, NING SERVICE will continue to drive innovation in maintenance technology, service models and network expansion. The Istanbul center is the first step in Türkiye, with further network build-out and capability development to follow.

data.title: Asian Equities Fall as Anthropic's Blockbuster IPO Fails to Staunch AI Stock Selloff
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities fell Friday morning as Anthropic's blockbuster initial public offering failed to staunch the selloff in artificial intelligence stocks.

"The central story was the paradox of a record-breaking AI-sector IPO failing to arrest a broader market selloff," Commerzbank Research analysts said in a report. "Rather than acting as a rising tide, the listing appeared to trigger rotation out of existing AI-related names as investors redeployed capital into the new issue," they said.

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, raised about $81 billion in the largest IPO on record, ending the overnight session with a market capitalization of roughly $1.3 trillion.

Anthropic shares opened more than 30% above their $83 IPO price, though gains moderated during the session to finish up 17% at $97.17 in their market debut. The pullback "coincided with declines in other AI-related stocks amid concerns about how higher interest rates affect technology valuations," said Antonio Di Giacomo, senior market analyst at XS.com, in an email.

The SPDR Select Sector Technology exchange-traded fund, which tracks the tech industry group of the U.S.' S&P 500, entered bear-market territory on Thursday, closing 1.9% lower at $160.69, more than 20% below its October peak.

Across Asia, South Korea's Kospi slid 4.7%, with chip-making index heavyweights SK Hynix shedding 6.3% and Samsung Electronics losing 4.8%. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average slipped 4.7%, as AI proxy SoftBank Group fell 15.6%, memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings dropped 12.6%, and Advantest, a manufacturer of automatic test equipment for the semiconductor industry, declined 12.3%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 benchmark index was down 0.9%.

Short-dated Asian and U.S. government bonds rose in price terms Friday morning as the equity-markets' selloff bolstered safe-haven demand for sovereign debt.

Yields on Australia's two-year government bonds declined 4 basis points to 4.6150% and on New Zealand's two-year sovereign notes fell 2 basis points to 3.8740%. U.S. two-year Treasury yields edged 2 basis points lower to 4.7429%% following Thursday's Treasury yield declines. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

"Risk aversion intensified, driving demand for U.S. Treasurys," two strategists at OCBC Group Research said in a report. "Investors continued to unwind crowded positions and reassess the macro outlook as Anthropic's record IPO sharpened scrutiny of stretched AI valuations and financing risks," the strategists added.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

data.description: NextDC's decision to sell undeveloped residential sites doesn't surprise its bull at Citi. Analyst Siraj Ahmed says his growth calculations for the Australian data-center operator already excluded its S5 and M5 sites, which could be sold. Ahmed tells clients in a note that NextDC's move to upgrade its Ebitda guidance by 5% at the range midpoint is a positive since it shows existing projects are on track. Less pleasing to him are the expected one-off costs related to the power delay at its M3 site and warding off potential acquirers. Citi has a last-published buy rating on the stock and a target price of 12.75 Australian dollars. Shares are down 4.7% at A$9.24. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)

data.title: Hertz Bank Lenders Form Group as Financial Risks Mount — WSJ
data.description:
By Samantha Kroontje, Jodi Xu Klein and Alexander Gladstone

Hertz's bank lenders are organizing as the struggling car-rental company confronts coming debt maturities, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

Barclays, which serves as the administrative agent for Hertz's revolving credit facility, has engaged Lazard as financial adviser and Milbank as legal counsel, the people said. The bank is circulating draft cooperation agreements aimed at binding revolving lenders together and preventing them from selling their loans at steep discounts to distressed investors, the people said.

Some of the revolver lenders have recently sold their positions, the people said.

Hertz has been struggling under its overbuilt electric vehicle fleet and has been exploring options to restructure its debt. The company has retained Latham & Watkins and PJT Partners for advice about its nearly $18 billion of debt, the people said. A group of senior secured creditors have hired Gibson Dunn and Evercore, the people said.

Hertz, Barclays and PJT declined to comment. Representatives for Lazard, Milbank, Latham, Gibson Dunn and Evercore didn't immediately respond to requests seeking comment.

Hertz emerged from chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2021. The restructuring, which followed a collapse in its rental business during Covid-19, helped Hertz trim down its debt load and allowed it to capitalize on a travel rebound after the pandemic. The company benefited from a strong rental market and improved used-car prices.

But its aggressive bet on electric vehicles pressured its business. Hertz in recent years has pulled back from its EV expansion. While Hertz's underlying rental business is improving, it continues to burn cash as it grapples with a heavy debt load and coming maturities. Hertz burned through more than $340 million in cash over the nine months ended September.

Revenue rose roughly 5.6% for the quarter that ended Sept. 30, compared with a year earlier, the company said. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization increased 15% in the period, but it fell short of expectations as weaker international demand and higher expenses weighed on results, it said.

The rental-car company said it ended the quarter with roughly $946 million in liquidity and expects to end the year with about $800 million after repaying $200 million of senior unsecured notes maturing this December.

Hertz Chief Financial Officer Scott Haralson said the company has sufficient liquidity to operate the business.

Its shares have tumbled more than 45% since the beginning of September to close at $1.23 on Thursday.

data.title: China Keeps Benchmark Lending Rates Unchanged
data.description:
China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged Friday, as it has for more than a year, as narrowing net interest margins deterred lenders from trimming borrowing costs despite weak credit demand.

The one-year loan prime rate was held steady at 3.0% and the five-year rate was unchanged at 3.5%, said the People's Bank of China. Both rates have remained at these levels since May 2025.

The LPRs are calculated each month based on submissions from 20 major commercial banks in China. The rates serve as the benchmark for most new and existing corporate and household loans in China.
